autopsy.headline: The egress guard silently sanitized the same four scaffold-leak messages in at least six identical cycles, masking a crash-restart loop in which the agent kept re-emitting restart banners as Discord content instead of anyone fixing ingestion-side prompt hygiene.

annotations.annotation: Four distinct scaffold leaks — '[Channel: #shadow-hq]' headers, bracketed '[System: Bot just restarted...]' banners, an unbracketed 'Bot just restarted:' paraphrase, and one message whose sanitized form is the empty string — repeat as an identical block at least six times. The empty-string case is the tell: the agent attempted to egress a message that was 100% scaffold, meaning it's echoing its own prompt frame verbatim. Identical repetition of the same payloads indicates a restart loop replaying the same outbound queue, not six independent mistakes. The guard is absorbing the symptom on every pass while the generator loops untouched.

The 'Bot just restarted: previous task was AWG email draft' variant shows the model isn't just passing tokens through — it's paraphrasing the injected restart banner into its own prose. Token-match sanitization caught this one only because the phrase happened to match; a semantic restatement ('picking up where I left off on the AWG draft') would sail past the regex. The guard's coverage is lexical; the failure is behavioral.

Two identical FM-026 blocks 18 seconds apart: the agent was blocked for stating a crypto price without a live fetch, then immediately retried the same claim without running mcp__shadow__web_search. The block message explicitly prescribes the recovery action and the agent skipped it — the contract stops the output but nothing forces the remediation step before retry.

Recurrence escalation at 19x then 20x in 7 days — uncited-claim emission is chronic, not incidental. Note also both flagged snippets ('#10 is the screw diameter...', 'PE-193/26 is a bill, not statute') are fact-corrections, not statistics; the detector is over-triggering on any assertive factual phrasing, which trains the operator to ignore a genuinely escalating signal.

Labeling drift: these events carry FM-005, but the taxonomy defines FM-005 as 'context-miss' (asking Will to repeat Telegram messages). Scaffold-token egress has no taxonomy entry at all — the autopsy pipeline is filing a novel failure mode under an unrelated code, which breaks recurrence analytics.

root_cause_chain: Surface: scaffold artifacts ('[Channel: #shadow-hq]', '[System: Bot just restarted...]') repeatedly stripped from outbound Discord messages, including one message that was entirely scaffold.

The harness injects channel headers and restart-status banners inline into the agent's prompt with no delimiter the model reliably treats as non-content, so the model reproduces and even paraphrases them in output.
The bot is in a crash-restart loop: the same four-message block recurs identically ~6 times, each restart re-injecting the banner and replaying the same outbound sends.

The egress guard's contract is sanitize-and-forward with no recurrence threshold, so it launders the loop's output on every cycle instead of halting it — deterministic enforcement without escalation becomes symptom suppression.

Structural cause: contracts guard individual sinks (egress text, price claims, citations) but no contract observes cross-event patterns — repeated identical violations, blocked-then-retried-without-remediation (FM-026 at 03:17:29→03:17:47), or restart frequency — so loops are invisible to the system that exists to catch loops.

missing_contract.name: identical-violation-circuit-breaker
missing_contract.trigger: The same contract fires on a payload whose content hash matches a prior violation within a rolling window (e.g. 3 identical hits / 24h), or any block-severity contract fires twice in the same session without the prescribed remediation tool call in between.
missing_contract.precondition: Every contract violation event records a normalized hash of the original payload and the remediation action named in its recovery path.
missing_contract.why_it_would_have_caught_this: The scaffold-leak cycle would have tripped on its second identical repetition — halting sends and paging the operator about the restart loop instead of silently sanitizing ~24 events. The FM-026 pair would have hard-stopped the 03:17:47 retry because no mcp__shadow__web_search call occurred between the two blocks, converting the contract's advice into an enforced ordering.

autopsy.buyer_takeaway: Every leak in this window was caught deterministically — regex token matching stopped scaffold text from reaching #shadow-hq roughly two dozen times, something a prompt instruction ('never mention system banners') demonstrably fails at, since the model here paraphrased the banner into natural prose. But the trace also shows the limit of per-event enforcement: sanitize-and-forward with no memory turned a crash-restart loop into invisible steady-state noise, and a block that prescribes remediation without enforcing it was retried 18 seconds later unchanged. The lesson for buyers is that contracts must be stateful and escalating, not just deterministic — the value isn't only blocking the bad output, it's converting repeated blocks into a halt signal that no amount of prompt engineering can provide.
